object_description: three-story school volume with a connecting base
design_condition: Placed in the southeastern part of the site parallel to the elevation curves, the complex uses two terrain levels and creates a generous enclosed open space, but appears crowded among its surroundings.

positive.statement: The independent open-space concept brings the entire complex together and creates a memorable place for the school and neighborhood.
A clear spatial organization and rational building structure enable a precise distribution of uses.
The primary level's courtyards, escape balcony and bright group rooms provide a high degree of flexibility.
The hybrid construction and moderate spans have a positive effect on primary energy and greenhouse-gas emissions.
The project achieves high architectural quality and contributes valuable spatial qualities for a new school.

negative.statement: The handling of the existing basement is unconvincing, and the missing transition between building and base creates a collage-like impression.
The new building appears crowded in its context and would become more self-evident as a solitaire.
The landscape treatment is didactic and directly implemented, while the uniform tree species contradicts the extensive-facility concept.
The entrances to the school area are all on the side and rather small.
The upper-level classrooms lack nearby storage and material rooms.
The caretaker's apartment location is not understood and seems anecdotal.
The poor compactness, low insulation values and high proportion of windows negatively affect energy efficiency.
The technical distribution and shaft concept remain unclear, with uncertain pipe routing.
The project has the highest construction costs because of its large amount of required space.
